advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the heal_multi_bundle call in push.py to also swallow/degrade non-S3DoctorConflict/OptionalDependencyError exceptions per the best-effort contract.
evidence: push.py:9 "ALWAYS returns ``None`` (best-effort): a push failure never fails the caller"
push.py:493-510 only `except s3_doctor.S3DoctorConflict` and `except OptionalDependencyError` are handled around `s3_doctor.heal_multi_bundle(base_path, remote, branch)`

s3_doctor._fold_heads calls `_lock.write_lock(...)` whose acquire can raise on timeout, and _publish_and_prune calls `s3.s3.put_object`/`delete_object` which can raise boto3 ClientError — none caught in push.py
advisory.finding: heal_multi_bundle's exception handling in push.py only catches S3DoctorConflict and OptionalDependencyError; any other exception raised during the heal (git failures, boto3/S3 client errors during download/put/delete, tempfile/OSError, write_lock timeout raising LockError) will propagate out of push_tickets_branch, violating its documented best-effort contract that a push failure never fails the caller and it ALWAYS returns None.
scenarios: S3 delete/put raises a transient boto3 ClientError during heal
write_lock cannot be acquired within _WRITE_LOCK_TIMEOUT and raises
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a broad `except Exception as exc:` arm (log + _raise_if_strict with a transport-failed reason + return) around the heal_multi_bundle invocation, mirroring the other terminal arms.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the acquire_lock exception handling to the helper's actual lock-conflict error type (or re-raise unexpected errors) instead of treating all exceptions as 'locked'.
evidence: s3_doctor.py: `try: lock_key = s3.acquire_lock(ref) except Exception: lock_key = None`

comment `# noqa: BLE001 - any raised error from acquire_lock means "locked"` asserts an assumption not guaranteed by boto3/git_remote_s3 which raise ClientError/EndpointConnectionError for many non-lock conditions
advisory.finding: acquire_lock is wrapped in a bare `except Exception` that treats EVERY raised error as 'locked', masking real failures (credential errors, network/S3 outages, bugs in the helper) as a benign no-op contention back-off.
scenarios: S3 credentials expired or bucket unreachable — heal silently returns healed=False reason=locked and the multi-bundle state persists forever

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Log/handle a delete_object failure in _publish_and_prune (record partial deleted_keys) rather than letting the raw exception escape unlogged.
evidence: s3_doctor.py comment: `# Let a delete raise (the merged tip is already durable).`
the delete loop `s3.s3.delete_object(...)` has no try/except; a failure aborts _heal_locked before the info log and before returning deleted_keys
advisory.finding: _publish_and_prune lets a delete_object failure propagate (documented as intentional since the merged tip is durable), but on such a mid-loop failure the previously-created scratch refs are cleaned up while the original bundles are left partially deleted and the function raises — the raised (non-S3DoctorConflict) error then escapes push.py's narrow handlers (see related finding), and no partial deleted_keys are reported/logged.
scenarios: First delete_object raises after the merged bundle was put — heal aborts with an uncaught exception and no summary log

advisory.finding: The push-path S3DoctorConflict branch (push.py lines 495-506) is never exercised by any test. The only push wiring test mocks heal_multi_bundle to return a healed result; no test drives the heal to raise S3DoctorConflict and asserts the resulting warning log, the push-multi-bundle-conflict reason passed to _raise_if_strict, or the early return. A regression in the reason code, the exc.hint plumbing, or the return would pass undetected.
merged_from: No test covers push-loop behavior when heal_multi_bundle returns a non-healed result (reason 'locked', 'noop', or 'remote-not-found'). The loop still sets healed_once=True and retries the push once; a regression that, e.g., loops forever or mis-handles the declined heal would not be caught.
scenarios: A push hits the multi-bundle state and the heal aborts on a non-derived conflict

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/enforce the precondition that base_path HEAD is one of the ref's bundle heads (or fold into a dedicated ref rather than the ambient HEAD).
evidence: s3_doctor.py _fold_heads: `merge-base --is-ancestor head_ref HEAD` and `git merge ... head_ref` operate against HEAD
push.py invokes heal with base_path being the tracker repo, and push pushes `HEAD:tickets` from a possibly-detached/ahead HEAD (push.py:6 'pushes HEAD:tickets (the detached-HEAD commit)')
ABSENCE: no assertion or reset ensuring HEAD equals one of the bundle SHAs before folding
dropped.finding: _fold_heads merges the fetched bundle heads into the tracker's CURRENT local HEAD rather than into a head derived solely from the enumerated bundles; the local HEAD is never verified to be one of the divergent bundle heads, so any local-only commits present in base_path get folded into and published as the merged tip.
scenarios: The tracker HEAD is ahead of / diverged from all remote bundle heads when heal runs; the published merged bundle then contains commits that were never accepted on the remote ref
